What is a 4% infection rate really costing?

Put a price on poor quality. In the app’s CLABSI worked example, a 4% infection rate means 48 infections and $2.3M a year; bringing it to 1% frees up $1.73M. That is a business case leaders act on.

Worst nurse on Monday. Best by Wednesday?

The Red Bead Ward simulation shows why daily league tables mislead: six nurses draw from the same box and the “worker of the day” changes by chance. Every point sits inside the control limits, so the differences come from the system.
